overview: IGO Limited is an ASX-listed Western Australian critical minerals company focused on the discovery, development and delivery of battery metals for electrification. Its two core exposures are (1) the wholly owned Nova nickel-copper-cobalt operation, which is in its final months of mine life and being divested to Global Lithium Resources for A$7 million once mining concludes (expected by end-calendar-2026), and (2) a 49% interest in the Tianqi Lithium Energy Australia (TLEA) joint venture with China's Tianqi Lithium Corporation, through which IGO holds an effective ~24.99% economic interest in the Greenbushes lithium mine (via TLEA's 51% of Talison Lithium, alongside Albemarle's 49%) and 49% of the Kwinana lithium hydroxide refinery. IGO divested its Tropicana gold interest in FY2021 and its Forrestania nickel operation in February 2026 to complete its transformation into a pure-play lithium/copper-focused battery metals business, with Greenbushes as the anchor asset funding a growth pipeline in copper (via proprietary BioHeap bioleaching technology) and further lithium opportunities.

business_model.summary: IGO's earnings are now dominated by its equity-accounted share of profit from TLEA (which owns Greenbushes and Kwinana), supplemented in the near term by nickel concentrate sales from the wholly owned Nova mine until it closes. Nova revenue is consolidated in the P&L, while the far larger and higher-margin Greenbushes/Kwinana earnings flow through as a single 'share of net profit of TLEA' equity-accounting line rather than as consolidated revenue - meaning IGO's reported group revenue substantially understates its true economic exposure to the lithium business. FY26 group revenue was A$463M (down 12% YoY, almost entirely Nova nickel concentrate sales), while the TLEA equity-accounted profit contribution was A$207.3M, more than the entire consolidated EBITDA base of the Nickel Business. Once Nova divests (expected by end of calendar 2026), IGO's income statement will be overwhelmingly a single-line pass-through of its TLEA equity interest, funded by dividends from Windfield Holdings (the entity that owns Talison/Greenbushes) periodically upstreamed to TLEA and then to IGO.

revenue_streams.name: Nova nickel-copper-cobalt concentrate sales
revenue_streams.description: A$448.9M FY26 revenue (of A$463M group total), EBITDA of A$158.4M at a 35% margin, cash costs of US/A$4.74/lb payable nickel (below guidance). Nova is in its final months of mine life (closure expected around December quarter 2026) and being divested to Global Lithium Resources for A$7M once mining ends; this revenue stream will cease entirely.

revenue_streams.name: Share of net profit from TLEA joint venture (Greenbushes + Kwinana)
revenue_streams.description: Not consolidated as revenue but equity-accounted: A$207.3M in FY26 (up from a A$642M loss in FY25, which included a large Kwinana impairment), reflecting Greenbushes' FY26 EBITDA margin of 73% (80% in Q4) on spodumene production of 1.41Mt (100% basis) at cash cost of A$415/t, partly offset by ongoing Kwinana refinery underperformance and negative contribution. This is the dominant driver of IGO's underlying NPAT and the primary determinant of intrinsic value going forward.

revenue_streams.name: Cosmos and Forrestania nickel (care and maintenance / divested)
revenue_streams.description: Cosmos nickel project remains on care and maintenance (FY26 underlying EBITDA loss of A$12.1M). Forrestania was placed into care and maintenance in October 2024 and its assets sold to Medallion Metals in February 2026 for a A$31.7M gain on sale, though IGO retained rights to explore/develop/mine nickel and lithium on the tenure.

business_model.customer_type: B2B commodity sales into global metals markets (nickel concentrate sold under offtake/smelting agreements; lithium spodumene and hydroxide sold to battery/cathode manufacturers, predominantly in China and Korea) - IGO is a price-taker on all products
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Western Australia operations (Nova near Fraser Range, Greenbushes in the South West, Kwinana near Perth), with product sold into global (predominantly Asian) battery supply chains. Corporate head office in South Perth.
business_model.margin_profile: Nova EBITDA margin ~35% in FY26 on high-grade ore but a maturing, cost-inflating asset near end of life. Greenbushes EBITDA margin 73% for FY26 (80% in Q4 FY26), among the highest in the global lithium industry, reflecting Tier-1 grade and scale. Kwinana Train 1 remains loss-making and below guided production (8,839t hydroxide vs 9,000-11,000t guidance) due to ramp-up and reliability issues; Train 2 construction has been halted indefinitely.

main_competitors: Mineral Resources (MIN.AX) - Wodgina and Mt Marion lithium plus mining services
Albemarle Corporation - IGO's co-owner in Talison/Greenbushes and a major global lithium chemicals producer/competitor
SQM (Sociedad Quimica y Minera) - Chilean brine-based lithium
BHP Nickel West / Wyloo Metals / other WA nickel producers (largely in care and maintenance)
Chinese lithium chemical converters and integrated players (Ganfeng, Tianqi's own operations, CATL-aligned resource plays)
competitive_position.market_position: IGO's Greenbushes interest gives it exposure to what is widely regarded as the world's largest, highest-grade and lowest-cost hard-rock lithium operation, but IGO itself is a minority, non-operating partner (24.99% economic interest via 49% of TLEA, which holds 51% of Talison; Albemarle holds the remaining 49% of Talison and Tianqi Lithium Corporation controls TLEA and Talison operatorship). IGO does not operate Greenbushes or Kwinana and has limited influence over key decisions (e.g., Kwinana Train 2 was paused by joint agreement with Tianqi, and Kwinana's future remains unresolved as of September 2026). In nickel, Nova was historically a top-quartile cost, high-grade underground operation, but it is now a wasting asset in its terminal months with no successor project in the current portfolio (Cosmos and Forrestania both in care and maintenance/divested).
competitive_position.market_share: Greenbushes alone supplies a globally significant share of hard-rock spodumene concentrate (historically among the top 2-3 sources of the world's spodumene supply), though IGO's own claim on that output is limited to its ~25% TLEA economic interest. Nova was a mid-tier global nickel producer (~15-17kt payable nickel in concentrate p.a.) but immaterial in global supply terms and about to exit the market entirely.

moat_factors.description: Greenbushes is widely regarded as the world's best hard-rock lithium deposit - exceptionally high grade, very low strip ratio in its updated pit design, low cash costs (~A$415/t spodumene in FY26) versus long-run industry price forecasts well above that level, and a Tier-1 EBITDA margin of 73-80%. This is a genuine, geology-driven cost advantage that is very difficult for higher-cost global peers to replicate.

Greenbushes' low unit costs mean it remains cash-flow positive and highly profitable even at depressed lithium prices that force higher-cost hard-rock and brine competitors into loss or care and maintenance - a durable structural cost advantage through the cycle.

IGO does not control Greenbushes, Talison or Kwinana. Tianqi Lithium Corporation is the controlling partner in TLEA and Talison's day-to-day operator; Albemarle is a large co-owner with its own interests. IGO's influence over capital allocation, expansion timing, and problem resets (e.g., Kwinana) is limited to its minority governance rights, creating genuine principal-agent and partner-alignment risk.

IGO's proprietary bioleaching technology could unlock low-grade copper sulphide resources otherwise uneconomic to process, providing a potential differentiated entry point into copper. Still unproven at commercial scale as of FY26, but management frames it as a genuine points-of-difference in future partnership negotiations.

IGO ended FY26 with A$386.5M cash, A$99.1M in marketable securities and an undrawn debt facility, giving it optionality to pursue growth opportunities and absorb further TLEA-related setbacks without financial distress.

weaknesses: Loss of its only wholly owned, cash-generating operating asset (Nova) by end of calendar 2026, leaving IGO with essentially one material earnings source (the TLEA equity interest) and a portfolio of pre-development/exploration assets - a significant concentration and diversification risk

No control over Greenbushes or Kwinana; strategic and capital decisions require alignment with Tianqi (and, for Talison specifically, Albemarle), and disagreements have already stalled Kwinana Train 2 and left Kwinana's future 'not yet resolved' as management states in the FY26 annual report

Kwinana Lithium Hydroxide Refinery has been persistently loss-making, underperforming production guidance, and was subject to a large FY25 impairment; downstream lithium chemical conversion in Australia faces structural competitiveness challenges versus Chinese processing that are not unique to Kwinana

Nickel Business has effectively been wound down (Cosmos on indefinite care and maintenance, Forrestania divested, Nova exiting) with no clear successor development project generating near-term production or cash flow

Growth pipeline (copper via BioHeap, further lithium opportunities, exploration in WA/NT/Arizona) remains largely pre-revenue and unproven, creating an earnings gap risk between Nova's exit and any new project reaching production

growth_drivers: Greenbushes Strategic Options Review with TLEA/Tianqi/Albemarle targeting improved productivity, mine planning and geotechnical optimisation, including a more compact, steeper pit design (reduced strip ratio, access to more resource) and the first underground lithia Mineral Resource estimate - management frames unlocking further value from Greenbushes as its single most important value-creation initiative

CGP3 (Chemical Grade Plant 3) ramp-up at Greenbushes, which contributed 104kt in FY26 despite a ~7-week outage from a June 2026 fire, with FY27 spodumene production guidance raised to 1,550-1,750kt (100% basis) from 1,410kt actual in FY26

Resolution of Kwinana Refinery's future - management and Tianqi continue discussions on a 'pathway forward' for Train 1, which would remove a persistent earnings drag if resolved constructively, though the outcome (continued operation, restructuring, or wind-down) remains uncertain

BioHeap proprietary copper bioleaching technology, which IGO is progressing toward proof at commercial scale and views as a potential differentiated entry point into copper, its stated primary growth commodity alongside lithium

Exploration portfolio across Western Australia, the Northern Territory and Arizona (copper-cobalt and nickel-copper-cobalt targets including Kimberley, Raptor, Irindina, Western Gawler, Adelaide Rift and Wolf), with capital and management attention increasingly directed toward the highest-quality opportunities after portfolio rationalisation

Improving lithium price environment through FY26 (realised spodumene price rose from US$1,668/t in Q3 FY26 to US$2,286/t in Q4 FY26) and industry-wide supply discipline (Western Australian nickel and higher-cost lithium producers curtailing output) potentially supporting a cyclical recovery that would flow disproportionately to Greenbushes' high margins

Nova divestment proceeds and cost avoidance (transferring closure/rehabilitation risk to Global Lithium Resources for consideration including deferred payment) frees management and capital for growth opportunities rather than end-of-life mine management

Disciplined capital allocation framework (2025 Capital Management Guideline) balancing growth investment with shareholder returns - FY26 final dividend reinstated at 5 cents per share after a nil FY25 dividend, signalling confidence in the post-Nova earnings base

business.risk: Post-Nova earnings concentration in a single, non-controlled asset
business.description: Once Nova exits (expected around December quarter 2026), IGO's income statement becomes almost entirely dependent on its 49% TLEA equity interest (an effective ~24.99% Greenbushes economic interest), an asset IGO does not operate or control. There is no committed, revenue-generating replacement project in the current portfolio.

Kwinana Train 1 continues to underperform (8,839t FY26 vs 9,000-11,000t guidance), conversion costs remain elevated (A$18,379/t vs A$16,000-20,000/t guidance), and Train 2 works have been halted. Management states explicitly in the FY26 annual report that discussions with Tianqi on the asset's future are 'ongoing and not yet resolved' and that broader structural challenges affect Australian lithium chemical conversion competitiveness industry-wide, not just Kwinana.

business.risk: Nova mine closure execution and transition risk
business.description: Nova must complete mining safely, manage workforce transition/redundancies, and complete the divestment to Global Lithium Resources (A$7M total consideration including deferred payment) on schedule; the transaction only takes effect once mining concludes, with completion targeted by 30 November 2026 (extendable to 15 December 2026).

As a 49% (minority-influence) partner in TLEA alongside controlling partner Tianqi Lithium Corporation, and with Albemarle as the other large Talison shareholder, IGO's ability to drive strategic outcomes (capital allocation, Kwinana resolution, expansion timing) depends on alignment across three large, differently-motivated shareholders - a structural governance constraint evidenced by the stalled Kwinana Train 2 decision.

BioHeap copper technology remains unproven at commercial scale, and the broader exploration portfolio (WA, NT, Arizona) is pre-development. Converting this pipeline into producing, cash-generative assets within a reasonable timeframe to replace Nova's contribution is unproven.

financial.description: IGO is a price-taker on nickel, copper, cobalt and lithium products, all priced in USD, with no commodity hedging undertaken during FY26 (per its Financial Risk Management Standard, hedging is only used to mitigate perceived risk, not for speculation). AUD:USD movements affect both metal sale proceeds and USD-denominated dividends received from the Lithium Business.

TLEA's share of net profit swung from a A$642M loss in FY25 (driven by a large Kwinana impairment) to a A$207.3M profit in FY26, illustrating how volatile and impairment-sensitive this single equity-accounted line can be - and how central it now is to IGO's reported results.

FY26 dividend was reinstated at 5 cents per share (FY25: nil) versus 37 cents in FY24 and 74 cents in FY23, reflecting the step-down in cash generation as Nova winds down and lithium prices/TLEA distributions remain below prior peaks; sustaining or growing the dividend depends on Greenbushes cash distributions and the pace of growth capital deployment.

regulatory.risk: Mine closure, rehabilitation and heritage obligations
regulatory.description: Nova's FY26 EBITDA included a A$15.5M increase to its rehabilitation provision plus A$15.0M in retention/redundancy provisions tied to end-of-mine-life; Forrestania's divestment included discharge of rehabilitation obligations. Ongoing compliance with Traditional Owner agreements (e.g., the Ngadju Nova Mining Agreement) and heritage protection remains a continuing obligation through closure.

regulatory.risk: ESG, climate and evolving disclosure requirements
regulatory.description: FY26 was the first year IGO reported under the AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures standard, reflecting rising compliance costs and scrutiny. The company also flags evolving community expectations and ESG legislation as material external risks.

regulatory.risk: M&A and asset transaction regulatory clearance
regulatory.description: The Nova divestment to Global Lithium Resources required ACCC review, which granted a notification waiver (unconditional as of 23 September 2026), illustrating that even smaller domestic transactions face competition-regulator scrutiny.

macro.risk: Nickel price collapse and industry-wide WA care and maintenance
macro.description: A global nickel supply glut (driven substantially by low-cost Indonesian supply) drove prices to multi-year lows in 2023-24 and forced widespread care and maintenance across Western Australia's nickel sector, including BHP's Nickel West/Kalgoorlie Nickel Smelter (suspended, under review with a decision due by February 2027) and Wyloo Metals' Kambalda assets. Nova avoided this fate only by being unusually low cost, but the broader WA nickel industry structure remains impaired, with no clear near-term price recovery catalyst.

Lithium spodumene/carbonate prices fell sharply from 2022-23 highs before stabilising and improving through FY26 (realised spodumene price rose from ~US$1,668/t in Q3 FY26 to ~US$2,286/t in Q4 FY26; carbonate around US$18,000/t and spodumene concentrate near US$2,000/t as of mid-2026). Given TLEA/Greenbushes now drives the large majority of IGO's earnings, IGO's valuation is highly geared to the pace and durability of any lithium price recovery.

Lithium and nickel demand are both ultimately tied to global EV and battery storage adoption rates; any slowdown in China EV demand growth or delayed grid-storage buildout would pressure both of IGO's core commodity exposures simultaneously.

IGO explicitly flags evolving global geopolitical tensions, trade policy shifts and tariff/import-export framework changes as external risks capable of influencing commodity prices, disrupting supply chains and impacting market access, relevant given China's central role as both a JV partner (Tianqi) and the dominant lithium chemical conversion and battery manufacturing market.

execution.description: FY26 saw significant leadership change: a new Non-executive Chair (Dr Vanessa Guthrie, from January 2026), multiple director departures/appointments, and CFO instability - Kathleen Bozanic departed, successor Johan van Vuuren resigned shortly after starting, with Ian Rowe stepping in as Interim CFO. This concentration of change at both Board and CFO level during a critical strategic transition (Nova exit, Kwinana resolution) elevates execution risk.

CEO Ivan Vella (appointed December 2023) has driven a two-year reset - Forrestania and Cosmos to care and maintenance/divestment, Nova to planned exit, exploration portfolio rationalisation - but the 'next chapter' (copper via BioHeap, further lithium growth) is explicitly still being built out and unproven, per management's own FY26 commentary that this next phase 'will look different from the one that built Nova.'

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global demand for lithium and copper is expected to grow structurally on electrification, energy storage and grid infrastructure buildout, but both markets are currently digesting the aftermath of 2022-2023 price spikes that triggered a wave of new supply, followed by 2023-2025 price collapses that forced widespread curtailment (WA nickel sector) and slower lithium capacity growth. Lithium carbonate/spodumene prices improved through 2026 (spodumene concentrate around US$2,000/t, carbonate around US$18,000/t by mid-2026) with some forecasters projecting a market deficit developing into late 2026 as delayed greenfield lithium projects and rising battery/storage demand converge, though long-run consensus mid-cycle price forecasts remain well below 2022 peaks.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High. Both nickel and lithium are highly cyclical commodities with a history of boom-bust price swings of several multiples in a few years. IGO's earnings (via Nova historically, and via TLEA/Greenbushes going forward) are directly and heavily geared to these cycles, amplified by Greenbushes' operating leverage (73-80% EBITDA margins mean profit moves close to one-for-one with price).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low to moderate direct sensitivity given IGO's strong balance sheet (net cash position, undrawn debt facility), but rate movements affect AUD:USD which in turn affects both metal sale proceeds and USD-denominated TLEA dividends.
key_input_costs: Labour and contractor costs (WA mining sector wage inflation)
Diesel, energy and consumables for mining and processing
Sea freight, smelting and refining/treatment charges for nickel concentrate
Capital costs for Greenbushes expansion/optimisation (sustaining, growth and deferred waste capex of A$355.7M in FY26, 100% basis) and Kwinana improvement works
macro_factors.currency_exposure: IGO's functional currency is AUD, but it is exposed to AUD:USD movements through USD-denominated metal sales and USD-denominated dividends received from the Lithium Business (TLEA). No currency or commodity hedging was undertaken in FY26 under the Group's Financial Risk Management Standard, which explicitly permits hedging only to mitigate perceived risk, not for speculation.

recent_developments.event: ACCC granted a notification waiver, making Global Lithium Resources' acquisition of the Nova Nickel Operation unconditional; completion expected within 10 business days of the first applicable trigger, no later than 30 November 2026 (extendable to 15 December 2026).

FY26 annual report released: group revenue A$463M (-12% YoY, Nova-driven), reported net profit after tax A$145.3M (vs a A$955M loss in FY25), underlying NPAT A$109.1M (vs -A$173.3M in FY25), underlying EBITDA A$285.9M, underlying free cash flow A$134.0M (+176% YoY), share of TLEA net profit A$207.3M (vs -A$642M in FY25). Final dividend of 5 cents per share reinstated after a nil FY25 dividend. Cash of A$386.5M and undrawn debt facility.

IGO announced the divestment of the Nova Nickel Operation to Global Lithium Resources (via subsidiary GL13 HoldCo No 3 Pty Ltd) for total consideration of A$7 million (cash, shares and deferred payment), conditional on completion of mining. Global Lithium intends to repurpose the Nova processing plant to treat ore from its Manna Lithium Project from mid-2027.

Fire at the Greenbushes CGP3 (Chemical Grade Plant 3) facility took the plant offline for approximately 7 weeks during ramp-up; production recommenced in early August 2026. Despite the incident, Greenbushes finished FY26 within its revised guidance range and delivered an 80% EBITDA margin in the June quarter.

Completed divestment of the Forrestania Operation assets (including the Cosmic Boy plant) to Medallion Metals, generating a A$31.7M gain on sale and discharging rehabilitation obligations, while IGO retained rights to explore, develop and mine nickel and lithium on the tenure.

Board renewal: Dr Vanessa Guthrie AO joined the Board in December 2025 and became Non-executive Chair from 1 January 2026, succeeding Michael Nossal (resigned effective 1 January 2026); Dean Jenkins joined the Board in February 2026.
CFO instability: Kathleen Bozanic departed as CFO; successor Johan van Vuuren resigned shortly after starting; Ian Rowe (an internal finance executive) appointed Interim CFO in June 2026.

IGO and Tianqi agreed to halt further construction works on the Kwinana Lithium Hydroxide Plant 2 (Train 2), redirecting capital toward Train 1 improvement projects; the broader future of the Kwinana Refinery, including a potential path forward, remains under active but unresolved discussion between the JV partners as of the FY26 annual report.

Company-wide safety turnaround: Group TRIFR fell 64% from 10.2 to 3.7 over the year, with Nova recording over 200 days without a recordable injury by year end - management highlighted this as evidence of broader operational discipline improvement across the business.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Ivan Vella characterized FY26 as 'a defining year' completing a two-year reshaping of IGO for 'a future beyond Nova,' citing strengthened leadership, rebuilt technical/commercial capability and a broader range of growth options, while acknowledging 'much of this work isn't yet visible externally.' Management's stated FY27 priorities are to safely complete Nova mining and support an orderly transition/divestment, improve operational performance and unlock further value at Greenbushes via the Strategic Options Review, maintain strong capital discipline, progress high-quality growth opportunities in copper and lithium, and continue strengthening organisational capability. On Kwinana, management was explicit that the conversation with Tianqi on the refinery's future 'is ongoing and not yet resolved,' and that sustainable long-term downstream lithium processing in Australia requires not just stronger prices but operating and capital structures capable of delivering acceptable returns through the cycle. The Chair reiterated confidence that Greenbushes 'remains a Tier 1 asset with exceptional margins' despite the FY26 CGP3 fire, and that ongoing value-optimisation work will further strengthen performance.

bull_case: Greenbushes is a genuinely world-class, low-cost (A$415/t cash cost), Tier-1 hard-rock lithium asset delivering 73-80% EBITDA margins even through a depressed pricing cycle - IGO's ~25% economic interest provides leveraged exposure to any lithium price recovery, with realised spodumene prices already rising from ~US$1,668/t to ~US$2,286/t through FY26 and some forecasters projecting a market moving into deficit by late 2026

Clean balance sheet (A$386.5M cash, A$99M marketable securities, undrawn debt facility, net cash position) provides resilience and optionality to fund growth or withstand further commodity weakness without dilution or distress

Nova divestment removes closure liability and cost burden from a wasting asset near the end of its economic life, while FY26 demonstrated Nova could still outperform guidance (production above, costs below) right up to closure, reflecting strong operational execution

FY27 Greenbushes production guidance raised materially (1,550-1,750kt vs 1,410kt FY26 actual) alongside lower guided capex (A$250-300M vs A$355.7M FY26), suggesting the capital-intensive CGP3 ramp-up phase is largely behind the joint venture and the asset should generate more distributable cash from here

Growth optionality via BioHeap proprietary copper bioleaching technology and a genuine exploration pipeline (WA, NT, Arizona) gives IGO a credible, if early-stage, path to a second growth leg in copper, IGO's stated primary target commodity alongside lithium
Dividend reinstated (5 cents per share FY26 final) after a nil FY25 payout, signalling Board confidence in the post-Nova, TLEA-driven earnings base and capital management framework
bear_case: Post-Nova, IGO becomes almost entirely dependent on a single, non-controlled equity interest (49% of TLEA, itself only 51% of Talison) - a significant concentration risk with governance and alignment constrained by two other large partners (Tianqi as controller, Albemarle as large co-owner), as evidenced by the unresolved multi-year Kwinana impasse

Kwinana Lithium Hydroxide Refinery remains a persistent value-destroyer: Train 1 has missed production guidance for multiple years, Train 2 construction has been halted, and management's own words are that the path forward 'is ongoing and not yet resolved' - a continuing source of downside earnings and capital-allocation risk with no clear resolution timeline

IGO's earnings history is extremely volatile and cyclical - the swing from a A$955M net loss in FY25 to A$145M net profit in FY26 was driven almost entirely by commodity price and impairment reversals rather than structural improvement, underscoring how exposed the stock is to nickel and lithium price cycles it cannot control

No committed, revenue-generating replacement asset exists for Nova once it closes (expected around December quarter 2026); Cosmos remains on indefinite care and maintenance, Forrestania is divested, and the growth pipeline (BioHeap, exploration) is pre-revenue and unproven at commercial scale, creating a potential multi-year earnings and cash-flow gap outside of TLEA distributions

Executive and Board turnover during a critical strategic inflection point (new Chair, multiple director changes, two CFO changes within roughly a year) raises execution risk at precisely the time IGO needs to negotiate Kwinana's future, execute Nova's transition, and stand up new growth projects

The Western Australian nickel sector remains structurally impaired industry-wide (BHP Nickel West suspended with a decision pending by February 2027, Wyloo's Kambalda assets on care and maintenance), illustrating that the price environment which forced Nova's exit is a genuine multi-year, not transient, feature of the nickel market - offering no near-term prospect of IGO re-entering nickel production profitably even if it wanted to
